title: Add integration test harness for ephemeral VPC (create/validate/destroy)
author: Sahana Iyer
body: Summary: This PR introduces an integration test harness that provisions an ephemeral AWS VPC using our alpha modules, validates a small set of expected invariants/outputs, and then tears everything down. The goal is to catch provider/module drift and unsafe defaults earlier than design partner pilots (e.g., subnet mapping, NAT assumptions, endpoint/DNS regressions). Motivation/Context: Unit-level terraform validate/tflint/checkov are necessary but not sufficient; we’ve already had issues that only show up once AWS resources exist (e.g., AZ assumptions, route association wiring, endpoint private DNS behavior). This harness is a minimal “smoke” environment that deploys modules the way customers will via examples, with assertions for the outputs the installer expects downstream. What’s included: (1) A Go-based Terratest suite under test/integration/ that runs terraform init/apply against examples/integration/ephemeral-vpc and performs basic assertions. (2) A dedicated example config (ephemeral-vpc) that composes modules/vpc + modules/endpoints + modules/logging with the smallest viable set of variables. (3) GitHub Actions workflow .github/workflows/integration-tests-ephemeral-vpc.yml that assumes an AWS role in the sandbox account via OIDC, runs the tests, and always attempts teardown (defer destroy). (4) Guardrails: unique name prefix per run, TTL tags on all resources, and a best-effort cleanup job to reduce orphan risk on cancelled runs. (5) Documentation in the repo README for how/when to run integration tests and the expected CI cost/time. CI/Cost/Runtime notes: Running this on every PR is expensive (AWS costs + ~18–30 min runtime depending on region/AZ capacity). Current proposal in this PR: run nightly on main + allow manual workflow_dispatch for maintainers and release candidates. We still keep fmt/validate/tflint/checkov gating per-PR (already in progress under ENG-4837 / PR-18503). Validation assertions (current set): VPC is created with expected CIDR; public/private subnets count matches inputs; private subnets have a route to NAT (when enabled); VPC endpoints created for S3/ECR API/ECR DKR/STS/CloudWatch Logs; endpoint security group is present; flow logs destination is created when enabled; key outputs are non-empty (vpc_id, private_subnet_ids, endpoint_sg_id). Notably we’re not asserting exact route table IDs or full endpoint policy JSON to avoid brittle tests; we’re targeting invariants that map to common pilot failures. Follow-ups (not in this PR): Add a second scenario for “no-NAT + endpoints-only” topology; add an assertion for private DNS settings (enabled/disabled) once we lock defaults with Security; wire a weekly budget report for sandbox account spend; consider moving from Terratest to terraform test once we’re on a baseline Terraform version across customers. Screenshots/Logs: See workflow run output for a full terraform plan/apply log; by default we redact AWS account IDs and do not print full state. Reviewer checklist: Please focus on (a) safety of the teardown paths, (b) whether assertions align with what the installer actually needs, and (c) whether the workflow scheduling is acceptable for alpha (nightly + manual).
commits: test(integration): add terratest harness for ephemeral VPC example
ci: add nightly + manual GitHub Actions workflow for integration tests
docs: document integration test usage and sandbox assumptions
chore: add TTL tagging helpers + cleanup safety net
notable_snippets: Workflow scheduling: `on: { schedule: [cron: '17 3 * * *'], workflow_dispatch: {} }` and uses OIDC role assumption for the sandbox account.
Terratest teardown: `defer terraform.Destroy(t, terraformOptions)` plus a final cleanup step guarded by `if: always()` in the workflow.
TTL tags: all resources created via examples include `tags = merge(var.tags, { "redwood:ttl_hours" = "12", "redwood:owner" = "ci-integration" })`.
conversation: Victor Alvarez (review): Nice. Two questions: 1) Are we comfortable with Terratest here vs terraform test? 2) Can we avoid validating route table IDs directly (brittle across AWS)?

Sahana Iyer (author): Agree on brittle assertions — this PR only checks presence of NAT route on private RTs (0.0.0.0/0 -> nat_gw) and avoids ID matching. On terraform test: we can revisit once we standardize TF >= 1.6 across module consumers; Terratest is easiest today with our pinned provider matrix.
Sean Gallagher (review): Teardown safety: what happens if the job is cancelled mid-apply? We’ve had orphaned NAT GWs before.

Sahana Iyer (author): Added TTL tags + a follow-up cleanup job that runs `terraform destroy` with best-effort even when earlier steps fail. Cancelled runs are still a risk, but TTL tags let us sweep in the sandbox account; also the workflow uses `concurrency` to prevent overlapping runs stomping on the same prefix.
Irene Choi (review): Runtime/cost needs to be explicit. Can we keep this nightly only for now, not per-PR? Also please ensure the role is limited to the sandbox account + specific regions.
Sahana Iyer (author): Updated workflow to nightly + manual only; added `AWS_REGION` allowlist in the workflow and tightened the IAM role policy doc reference (INT-1734).
Devon Price (review): One nit: please redact terraform output that includes account IDs. Also consider splitting logs for easier debugging.
Sahana Iyer (author): Done — reduced verbosity, removed printing of caller identity, and added a short summary section at the end of the job with key outputs only.
Irene Choi (final): Approved after tightening scheduling + region allowlist. Please open a follow-up for a second scenario (endpoints-only).
Sahana Iyer (author): Will do; added to ENG-4860 subtask list.
ci_checks: checkov: pass (1 skipped: CKV_AWS_### for example-only public subnet IGW route; documented rationale in example README)
merge_outcome: Merged (squash) by Irene Choi into main; workflow left as nightly + workflow_dispatch to control spend during alpha; follow-up requested to add endpoints-only scenario and periodic sandbox cleanup reporting.
